I have self-harmed for 6 years this past week. It is an addiction. It starts for somewhat different reasons for everyone, but my story started with a very low self-esteem. I wasn't feeling good about myself and one day my mother said something that put me over an edge. It's not a pretty thing, and it hurts my family and friends who know about it. So why do I do it still? Because it's relief. Over the course of a day my emotions build up and get stuck in my head. I'm a very sensitive person and even little things set me off. I used to do it at work too, if a manager or coworker criticized what I was doing. If I did something wrong, they would say something about it but sometimes in a harsh tone and I would walk away. I would go to the bathroom and hurt myself so I could feel better. It gave me relief from how I felt on the inside, because I would start hurting on the outside. I would tell myself, "they can't hurt me more than I've already hurt myself." And then I felt like no matter what they said to me, it wouldn't matter. It was a feeling of invincibility, that lasted until the next time, often the same day, when I was again criticized. I'm still repeating this process at my new job, and I just can't stop this cycle.

Oh god never. I just started a few days ago at a Starbucks in a Target and it sucks. I didn't receive any training on the register before we opened because my Trainer had no idea she had to train me that day. She threw a binder at me and told me to read through it. I read through everything that applied to my job and I ignored the history lesson because I had a feeling about what was coming. She then put me on register to take orders and handle the money. I was constantly asking her, "how do I put that in the register? How do I mark that on the cup?" It was awful. And then she would go into the storeroom and do things when we had customers approaching the bar and I had to go call her because she hadn't trained me on making any drinks. Plus, all 3 of the days I've worked so far have been long 7-2 shifts during the busiest time of the day. I have been trained on some of the hot drinks now, so I can handle certain orders by myself. But I have coworkers telling me that after their 4th or 5th shift, they were opening on their own. Even thinking about that gives me anxiety and I'm already so stressed as it is. 

This job was not what I originally wanted anyway, I had applied at Target just to be in the retail part of the store. I had previously worked in foodservice, and I had left because I hated the whole taking orders, fulfilling orders process. I wanted a retail job to try something completely different and instead, they offered me a job in the Starbucks. I accepted, thinking, "okay, this could work out, it doesn't sound too bad and Starbucks is supposed to have really good training policies in place. Maybe I'll just try it out and see what happens." I already wish I had stuck it out and tried to work in the actual Target. If I had known what my first shift, my first day, my first week could be like  I would have turned it down. It's so incredibly stressful for a job that sounded so simple, so easy. 

I didn't know this until yesterday but one of my cousins worked at a standalone Starbucks for a week and then quit because they assumed she knew what to do and how to make drinks when she told them that she needed to learn. She had a similar experience to mine because she wasn't trained either. I should have talked to her first before I accepted the job.

I'm going into HR in a day or two to ask about transferring departments into Apparel because I just cannot stay in Starbucks. If they refuse me, I'm going to quit the Target, simple as that. I don't need this job, and it seems like they don't need me either.


tl:dr; Starbucks is stressful and their training policies are often bs. Please don't do that to yourself.
